utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the late start. We propose to sit through at this stage until 4.00, take half an hour break and then sit through from half past 4.00 until 6.00. Bearing in mind that my two colleagues have already spent four and a bit hours in the Court today, I think that's about the limit of all of our endurances. Sir, would you please stand up, make the solemn declaration in the document which the usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, sir. Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, before we proceed, I think that we should give the witness name and surname of protected Witness VG118, because his testimony will concern the same events, so that he know who we are talking about and so that he can refer to the protected witness in question under the pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you have a pseudonym sheet that he can be given?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's 117, and if Mr. Domazet's sheet is incorrect, I have one with 117 on it. I believe the witness was 117.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It was --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. It was translated as 118.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Under 117, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. That will be Exhibit D48 and it will be under seal. Do proceed, Mr. Domazet. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djuric, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, I will be examining you today on behalf of the Defence team for Mitar Vasiljevic. I should like to ask you to answer my questions, but would you please bear in mind the need to pause before you begin your answer. I will also be mindful of that so that we can facilitate the work of the interpreters, especially in view of the fact that we speak the same language. Also, would you please be so kind and have a look at the piece of paper that is in front of you. Whenever I ask you a question about this particular person, or if you need to speak about her, would you please not mention her name or surname, but refer to her with the pseudonym, which is on the sheet of paper that is in front of you. So, Mr. Djuric, for the record, would you please state your name and surname, the name of your parents, and the place and date of your birth.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Djuric. I was born on the 15th of November, in Loznica, in the municipality of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your parents' names?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Miodrag Djuric. My mother's name is Ruza.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where do you currently reside, Mr. Djuric?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In Loznica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I shall now focus on the events from 1992. First of all, would you please tell me whether you lived in the village of Loznica at the time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, sir, the interpreters are having a little difficulty hearing you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The interpreters are having a little difficulty hearing you. Would you bring your chair just a little closer to the desk so that you are speaking right into the microphones. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, 1992, in Visegrad, sometime in the second half of May, you probably remember the fact that the Uzice Corps was in Visegrad at the time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what you did at the time, that is, what you did after the departure of the Uzice Corps.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Just as everybody else, I was demobilised into the army for the defence. I worked. I stood guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I think that you have misspoken, Mr. Djuric. Were you mobilised or demobilised at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who mobilised you, Mr. Djuric?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, politicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, Mr. Djuric? What kind of command, headquarters, or organisation was it? What was the institution that mobilised you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what kind of institution it was at the time. It was called the army of Republika Srpska. I mean, it is called the army of Republika Srpska today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me try to rephrase my question. At that time, in the period preceding that time, was there an organisation which was called Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There was the Territorial Defence. It existed even prior to that, I mean before we were ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At that time, did you have a uniform at home? Had you already been issued with a uniform? Did you take it there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I had a uniform at home at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What kind of uniform was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: An SMB, that is, an olive-drab uniform, the Yugoslav uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Once you were mobilised, where did you go and where did you usually spend your time after that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I went to the local community of Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was it there that you were issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you go somewhere else from there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We did, slowly, in order, towards Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the name of the locality? We don't have it in the record. We do now. Where is Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The place where our positions were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, I don't want to stop you from bringing in something which you may think is important, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- your case is really in response here to the additional material which the Prosecution was allowed to call in reopening its case. Now, this doesn't seem to me to have any relevance to that at all. If you think, however, that it's something very important to your case, we wouldn't stop you from proceeding, but I think we really do need to know why we're hearing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I thought that I would cover these preliminary issues much faster. This was just an introduction. My idea was to elicit from the witness the information about his residence at the relevant times. Let me try and wind this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, you were in the vicinity of the village of Rujiste at the time, on various locations, various positions. Were you at any point in time called back to Visegrad in order to receive a mission, an assignment, and go to a village? Could you tell us something about it, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was called back and told to go to the village of Gostilja. My task was to inform them about a convoy which was supposed to arrive the next day to transport them to Visegrad, and from there, further on towards Tuzla, in buses. And this is what I did. I went there. I informed them about that, and the next day everybody was rounded up on their own, of their own free will, without any force, according to their wishes. And so that is where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, would you please concentrate on my questions and try to be as brief as possible in your answers, and if necessary, I will ask you for clarification so that your answers can be as precise and as clear as possible. So if I understand you correctly, at one point in time you were called back from the front line and told to go to the village of Gostilja; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was there anyone else with you? Did anyone else go with you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Goran Ristic did, the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What were you told on that occasion? What were you supposed to say to those people in Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That they should gather the next morning, that trucks would be there to fetch them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say "the following morning," you meant the following day, the next day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So were you in Gostilja with trucks the following morning, together with this person by the name of Ristic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How many trucks or other vehicles were there on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There were three trucks and one --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't catch the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, the interpreters didn't get the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, what other vehicle did you have in mind, apart from these three trucks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: A Lada Niva, a passengers' car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who was at the wheel of this car, at the wheel of the Lada Niva?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Ristic was, Goran Ristic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about you? Where were you? In which vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In one of the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Apart from you, the driver of the truck and Goran Ristic, were there any other individuals in this group?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you arrived in Gostilja in this Lada Niva car, accompanied by three other trucks, and that was it, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So what happened once you arrived in Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The people had gathered, and then they boarded the trucks. As for the Niva, we also used it for the father and the mother-in-law. It was the Lada Niva that was used to transport these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you please be more precise, Mr. Djuric. Who was transported in this Lada Niva by Ristic from Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He transported VG, VG117, and her parents-in-law, the one who had a fractured leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: All others boarded the trucks that were in this group and you were in one of those trucks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know why Witness VG117 and her parents-in-law were transported in this car, unlike others who were in those trucks? Do you personally know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I do, because her brother-in-law was an officer. I don't know exactly whose officer, in which army, but he was in Belgrade, and that is why she had this privilege.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where did those vehicles go, and where did they eventually arrive?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They eventually arrived in Visegrad, in a local school, Vuk Karadzic School, where those people were put up, but these people had a different, separate accommodation, not the same one as others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, when you say they had separate accommodation, who do you have in mind, please? Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, everybody was placed in the gym, but they were in a separate classroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say that everybody was placed in the gym, you are referring to the people who had been transported in trucks, but I would like to know who was placed in the separate room, in one of the classrooms.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: VG117, her father-in-law, and her mother-in-law. They were placed in this classroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you came to the Vuk Karadzic school, and after the people had left the trucks, did they, I mean all of them, including the group which was in the Lada Niva, did they spend some time in front of the school or were they taken into the school, were they taken inside immediately?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They went inside immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At the time you arrived and at the time people started getting off the trucks, were there any other people in the school or outside the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Outside the school there was a group of about five or six people, but there was no one in the school. There was no one inside the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Those people who were in front of the school, were they civilians or soldiers, and did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I know they were Muslims. They were there because they knew we would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say that they knew you would come, were they actually waiting for someone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were waiting for their relatives. Those people were their relatives who lived in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you also remain in the school once they had been put up in various classrooms?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you remain there for the rest of the day, and did you leave the school building at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It is possible that I left for a very brief period of time, but I know that I spent there two nights and one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say that perhaps for a little while you were away, what time was that? What are you referring to exactly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps about 10, 20, 25 minutes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please tell us why would you be away for that time? What were you doing during that time, those 20, 25 minutes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, to get cigarettes, to go out and get something.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you spent that day there and two nights. Does that mean that you spent the following day there as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you personally armed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you carrying weapons the same that you were carrying when you were on your positions, or was this different, were these different weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The same weapons I had when I was on my positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What sort of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Besides yourself, during that time, were there other people carrying arms in the school? Were there policemen, were there soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, there were no soldiers, with the exception of myself and Ristic, and there were no other people carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: While you were in the school building, did the police secure the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did secure the school. It was, in fact, a patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What does that mean, on patrol, patrolling, Mr. Djuric?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they were moving. They visited the town. They were not located there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Please tell me: You said that Ristic was beside you. Did he also remain there the entire time, like you, or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If not, how long was he absent?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He was absent because he was driving the Lada Niva, and then VG117 returned to her village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Well, before we come to that, please describe how he returned and where. You said that he had been driving. Did he leave before then, and was he absent for any given time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, he was absent for short periods of time. He was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The people who came with you from Gostilja and who were put up in this school, these people, could they move around freely? Were they able to leave the school, come to the school, or did you have orders to make this impossible for them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They were free. They could move around freely. They could go into town. No one, in fact, prohibited them from doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were there also other people that came from town and who were also participating?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Before you you have the name of the witness whom we referred to as VG117 and about whom you said that she was with her parents-in-law. Did you know her before that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Perhaps. I know her from sight. I wouldn't know her now. And perhaps I did know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you know anyone else from that family?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I knew her husband only.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did she herself leave the school, abandon the school, while you were at the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, she did. She asked me if she could go to try to find her daughter, so as to have her by her side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did she tell you why her daughter was in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, she was married there in Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did she go and fetch her daughter?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, she did, and she returned with her daughter. And the daughter spent the night there with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see that personally? Did you see that her daughter had come, personally? Did you see her?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you by any chance talk to her daughter?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Just in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember any particular detail which was characteristic, which could characterise that meeting with her?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When I was referring to that, I meant how she was dressed, something that would draw attention to her.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, the daughter was wearing a leather suit, and I advised her in the meantime whether this was necessary, whether it was necessary for her to wear that suit, or was that any -- was she wearing that for any special reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you believed that wearing a leather suit was not appropriate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, because of her personal safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Because at the time there were all sorts of people in Visegrad, all sorts of armies that were unlawful, illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say, well, there were all sorts of soldiers, armies around that were illegal, you mean not the regular army but you're referring to some paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about the family of the witness, the daughter who had come, the parents-in-law. How long were they at the school? Were you there while they were at the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had spent the night. They couldn't find transportation to go back, and her brother-in-law, he was not able to come from Belgrade to take them over, so we took them to Ristici and Gostilja, where they spent the night at Miloje's, and the next day they went to Zaovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So if I understood you well, they had spent the night at school and the next day Ristic took them to Gostilja. How did Ristic take them to Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He put them up at Miloje's. Joksimovics, they spent the night there, and the next day they went to Zaovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you with them or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who told you that they had gone to Miloje's, and then that they had proceeded the next day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, Ristic told me that when he came back, that they had left them at Miloje's.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And this place that you're mentioning, Zaovina, where is it located and what does it represent? I didn't quite understand it. What is the name of the place that you mentioned that they left after having been to Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Zaovina. It's in Serbia. Zaovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What did Ristic tell you why these people had gone to Zaovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, we knew that the brother-in-law would wait for them there and would take them over, that he would come with his car, because he couldn't cross the border there, and that's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: A while ago you said that Ristic said before that that he wasn't able to find transportation. What was this about? What sort of transportation was he supposed to provide?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, we had that one car, and we used it for all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that he had to provide another car, and since he was not able to do, so he had to use the car in question; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The following day, when he had taken them, did the other inhabitants of Gostilja remain at the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What part of the day was it? At what time was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So following the departure of the people with Ristic, did you remain at the school and spend the night at the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at the school? Until when?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, until 10.00 the following day. Then I was ordered to return to Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that, in fact, mean that you returned to the unit from which you came two or three days earlier?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you returned to Rujiste, to your positions, did the other people from Gostilja remain in the school? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, I would like now to return to the first day when you came to the school and when all those who had come were placed in the school. Tell me: On that occasion, following your arrival, did someone else come to the school or in front of the school and write down the names of the people who had come to the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, no one came to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see in front of the school a table, some chairs, and at one moment, if there were such people, was there anyone sitting at that table and writing something down?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, no one was sitting there and no one was writing down the names of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that the whole time, with the exception of a short period of time, that you had remained there. Could it have been possible for someone to come and spend an hour or so there in front of the school and write down these names without your being able to notice it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, this was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember at all whether there was a table and chair in front of the school at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, there was nothing there. There was only the entrance to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The people who had come with you by trucks, did they spend any time in front of the school or did they go into the school straight away?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They went into the school straight away. They put their things there, their bags, and then they walked around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you confirm that other people could come and go as they pleased from that school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Not other people; just those people who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you something different. Do you personally know Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How long have you known him personally?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: From the fourth grade of elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? Do you belong to the same generation, or do you know him from sight, or did you go to the same grade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He was the generation older than me, but we went to the same school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: After you had finished school, did you continue seeing him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you explain to us where he was living, what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He lived in Kaleta. He worked as a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Until the period of 1992, did you see him frequently?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, not really frequently, because I was in the field and he worked more -- he worked in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you know him well enough to be able to recognise him anywhere you might see him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you see him today in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where is he, and is it the Mitar Vasiljevic we are referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He is behind your back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Behind my back, you mean my back?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We don't want to incriminate one of the security officers of the Tribunal, Mr. Domazet. I think you had better ask him what Mr. Vasiljevic is wearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said behind my back. Can you tell us what he is wearing? Perhaps you cannot see him from there.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He is wearing a white shirt, a tie, and a brown suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djuric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we can accept that he's now identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Djuric: In the period that you have described, from the time when you were mobilised until the present moment, when you were asked to go to Gostilja, did you see Mitar Vasiljevic on any occasion or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So during that specific period of time, did you hear anything about him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I did hear something about him, that he was in town. We were 40 kilometres apart. That is the distance between Rujiste and Visegrad. I heard a couple of days later that Mitar was in the hospital, that he had fallen from a horse.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say two or three days later that you heard that he was in the hospital, what are you referring to? Two or three days after what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: When I said -- two or three days later, I heard that he was in hospital.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat that. We didn't quite catch what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, the interpreters are still having troubles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please repeat. You said, "Two or three days later I found out that he was in hospital." You said two or three days after what did you hear that he was in hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Two or three days before I went to Gostilja, I found out that Mitar was in hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you found that out, did you know that he -- how many days had transpired before you learnt that he was injured?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: A couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is that with reference to the day that you found that out?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember, by any chance, who told you that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you the name of the person, but you know how soldiers are; they talk a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does it mean that you heard about that while you were still in Rujiste, at the front line?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you recall, by any chance, what date it was when you were ordered to go to Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you the exact date, but it was about that time. It was the harvest time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How do you know that, Mr. Djuric? Did you notice anyone working in the field?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I know it because I was harvesting as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said when you were up there, that the people were working in the field. Where exactly were you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, the day -- one day before I went to Gostilja, the day when I went to tell them that we would come the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you personally know in that area when is the harvest time? When does it start?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, there's more than one season, and it also depends on what you're harvesting. I think it is sometime in mid-June. That is the time when people usually make hay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you say that in mid-May people begin to make hay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Witness 117 said that it was on the 22nd of June, 1992, that they went to school. Is it possible that was the date in question, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't quite understand what you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, it may be an error in translation, but the witness thought that it was mid-June, and then you said: "If I understand you correctly, you say it was in mid-May ..." Now, I don't want there to be any error --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No. It's a mistake. It was perhaps mid-June. Yes, I saw that. Yes, yes. I'll ask it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps you had better ask it again, unless you suggest there is an error in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djuric, when you said that the people start making hay sometime in mid-June, did you mean -- did you refer to the area of Visegrad and that part of the country?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I said it depended; it depended on the kind of crop. There are things that you have to cut or mow earlier, some other grasses cut later on, but it would be thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me go back to what I asked you a moment ago and what you didn't quite understand. I was talking about Witness VG117. She said that she had come from Gostilja to the school in question on the 22nd of June. In view of what you have just said, would that date be the one on which it happened? Could that be the date in question?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, once again, I don't recall the exact date, but it would have been sometime in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You told us something concerning Mitar Vasiljevic, but let me ask you once again: During those days when you were in Vuk Karadzic school, did you at any point in time see Mitar Vasiljevic there, the person you described today and whom you said you knew very well? Did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know the person by the name of Milorad Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know where he's from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He's from Paocici.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know who his wife is? Do you know her name and where she is from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Milorad Ivanovic from Paocici, was he in Vuk Karadzic school or around the building? Did you see him there at any point in time while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that some police officers came. Can you remember, if you happen to know any of them, who it was that came?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Like I said, their patrol came. I knew the one who was there with me, Simsic and some other individuals as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you be more precise, please. You said you knew Simsic. Does it mean that one of the policemen who came to the school was Simsic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who else do you remember? Who else came to the school while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, you know how police work. After they finish their shift, they leave. Sometimes they would come during the night, this patrol that was visiting the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you remember anyone else apart from Simsic, anyone else that you knew personally?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: You know how it was. Those people were beginners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you mentioned Simsic, you said apart from Simsic and this one who was there with me. Who did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: But the one who's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you referring to the witness who has come with you here, who is here with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: While you were with this group of people in Vuk Karadzic school, before you went back to Rujiste, was there a paramilitary unit or a group of people that entered the school building? Did they do anything that you would have noticed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: While I was there, no one came.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Djuric. My name is Dermot Groome. I will be asking you --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- questions on behalf of the Prosecution. Mr. Djuric, if at any time I ask you a question you feel that your answer -- or answering it honestly may cause you problems or cause your Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. family problems, please bring that to our attention so that the Chamber may deal with it. Cira, your name -- most people know you by Cira; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that most people in Visegrad may not even know your first name as Zoran but would certainly know you as Cira?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to begin by asking you to tell us again with more precision about your visit to Veliki Gostilja. Can you tell us where is that village in relation to your village, Loznica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Six, maybe five kilometres away, in the direction of the Serbian border, in relation to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if you were travelling from your home to -- I'm sorry. If you were travelling from the town of Visegrad to the village of Loznica, would you have to pass the village of Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You told us that when you were mobilised, you were sent to Prelovo. Did you spend -- other than the time that you spent at the school, did you spend the remainder of your service in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. We were not in Prelovo. We were just mobilised there. There was an office there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when were you mobilised, as best you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: As best as I can tell, the 22nd, as soon as the Uzice Corps left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that would be the 22nd of April?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during your time in Prelovo, did you ever see Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In Prelovo? I heard that he was with the kitchen, and I didn't have any contact with the kitchen. They were further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you received your meals, did you ever see him delivering the meals to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. First of all, we didn't have any canteen. We ate on the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who brought you your food?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as the van could go, and from there, the food was transported in dishes. But I don't know who it was who actually transported the food.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So do you know the names of any of the people who transported food to where you were, outside of Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They couldn't come as far as our positions. I know that Vojnovic was driving this van, but who actually distributed the food, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe that van for us, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It belonged to the forestry. It had eight seats. Now it is painted red, but at that time it was blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anything else unusual about that van that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anything unusual or particular about the van that you can recall at this time? Was there any unusual damage to it? Did it make any unusual sounds as it was driven?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I never took a ride in it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You told us about you advising a young woman that she shouldn't wear a leather suit, and I believe you said that it was unsafe for her to do so. Can I take it that you gave her this advice because you were concerned for her safety?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I told VG117 - that's her daughter - that it was logical for them not to wear too much make-up, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to tell us specifically: What did you fear might happen to this young woman because she was wearing a leather suit or to these other women who were wearing make-up? What did you believe might happen to them, dressed in that manner?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: See, in my opinion, a rape, for instance, could have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So then you must have been aware at that time that --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: People are attracted by beauty, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, you must have been aware at that time that other women had been raped in Visegrad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So prior to your giving these women this warning, you were not aware of any women being raped or abused during this time period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that all sorts of armies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you've finished with that, before you go on, it may be important, might it not, in order to judge the -- what weight we give to this evidence what he means by a leather suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If we're worried about rapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Was it trousers or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to describe in a little greater detail what it was about the leather suit, the way it appeared, that made you believe it posed a danger for this young woman.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't have anything in particular in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat his answer. It's not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you, the interpreters are having trouble picking up your voice. I'd ask that you speak a little bit louder and into the microphone so that they can hear you a little bit better.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Was the bottom half of the suit, was it a dress or trousers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, when I say "suit," I mean a coat and a skirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the coat you're referring to, that was made of leather? Was the coat made of leather?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Both pieces were made of leather.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anything in particular about this suit that you thought would make it more likely that this young woman would be the victim of a rape?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There was nothing in particular, but the danger was always present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Let's go back a year before this. Had you seen this young woman in May or June of 1991 dressed in the same suit, would you have warned her and her mother that it was dangerous to wear such a suit in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So explain to us: What did you know -- what was going on at this time that made you give this warning to this young woman?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: First of all, she was not a young woman. She was a married woman. And the reason I gave my advice was because you cannot always protect yourself. I just didn't want her to cause any trouble for herself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you said around this same part of your testimony that there were all sorts of armies in Visegrad, and you said that those armies were not illegal -- were not legal, I'm sorry. Is it this group of people that you thought posed a danger to this woman?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, because of them. That is exactly why I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us everything you can about the illegal armies that you were aware of? Can you first tell us the names of the different illegal armies that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, first of all, I never encountered them. They were located some 40 kilometres away. I was in Rujiste, they were in Visegrad. I didn't personally know any of them, nor did I see any of them or meet with any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you testified earlier, I, for one, got the impression that you had some direct knowledge about these illegal armies, so I'd ask you: How did you know that there were these illegal armies in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It's not difficult to learn such things. People talk a lot. You hear all kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, will you tell us what you heard about these armies? What armies did you hear were in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Some kind of White Eagles. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Again, sir, I'd remind you: If there is something about your answer that you think could pose a problem to you, to you or your family, please advise the Court of your concern. Is the White Eagles the only illegal army that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There was a number of them, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were some of them from -- or do you know where they were from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We didn't know exactly. They had come from all parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: From parts in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, no. From various parts of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, your army that you were associated with, that was a legal army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've told us about several orders that you received. Did you ever receive an order, or are you aware of any soldiers such as yourself receiving an order to go into the town and to disarm these illegal armies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No one made any such attempts. The police was probably helpless.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would that be a good place to break, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. We'll resume at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, I'd like to return to the topic that we were talking about before the break and ask you -- maybe over the break you've had a chance to think about some of the paramilitaries that were present in Visegrad, and let me ask you a few questions in that regard. Did you ever hear of Seselj's men being in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of a group referred to as the Chetnik Avengers being present in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of any Serbian police being present in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about the police being there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, on this particular day, when you drove these people, or drove with these people from the village to the town, did you see any paramilitaries in the town on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't. I wasn't moving around town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, you did testify that you drove with the people from the village of Gostilja to the town of Visegrad, to the Vuk Karadzic school; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It's correct, but I was in the school building. I was walking around the building, and none of them came while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm talking -- I'm asking you to tell us: On the drive from Gostilja into -- or to the school, can you tell us what paramilitaries you saw on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw people I did not know. I didn't -- I don't know what paramilitary formations they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the people that you saw that you did not know, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how many people did you see that you did not know that were armed with weapons on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see them in groups. One or two individually were walking around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you afraid of these people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you left the school for a brief period of time and went to get a pack of cigarettes, I believe. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It was near the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But you went to get some cigarettes, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was near the school. It was close by. I didn't walk around the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you do for your food? How did you get food to eat during your time at the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We ate out of tins, dry food. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who brought you that food?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Ristic, with his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And he brought food for all of the people at the school or just for you and himself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Only for the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There was no food in the building itself, in the school, was there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would I be correct in thinking that at this point in time, the area around the school was mostly deserted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, not deserted. There were people around. Basically Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So at the time -- or you're saying that -- strike that, please. Are you saying that you saw Muslim houses or that you actually saw Muslim people in the area around the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Muslims and their houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during the entire time that you were at the school, can you give us an idea of approximately how many Muslims you saw in this neighbourhood around the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said that the people at the school were free to leave the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the time you were physically present at the school, can you tell us how many people did in fact leave the school and go to town or go to somewhere outside of the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they went to visit their family. They went visiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know where they went? Was it in the town or in this area of town?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In the area around town. They went to have something to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So approximately how many people from the school left the school and went somewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't leave completely. They would be away an hour or so and then come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, because of what you heard about the paramilitaries and because of what you saw, you saw some paramilitaries that day, would you have thought it safe for you yourself to walk into the town from the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I believe you told us that you were armed with an automatic gun at this point in time; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Semi-automatic gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it have been safe for any of the people inside the school to walk down to the town?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't go deep into the town, but whoever wanted to would go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, sir, is: Would it have been safe for, let's say, this woman in the leather dress to have walked into town to buy a pack of cigarettes or to buy some food? Would that have been safe for her?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't be safe, and that's why I was telling her not to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it have been safe for any of the people in the school to walk down to the middle of town to get some food or to get some cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It wasn't safe, but they went nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were in the school during the time that you were at the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: About a hundred people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And of those hundred, how many left the school at a certain point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they came and went. I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you when you received the instructions to leave Rujiste and to go to the village of Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who gave you the order to leave Rujiste and to go to this village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. Could you repeat your answer, please. Oh, the command.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us his name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Vinko Pandurevic was in command at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And he personally told you or gave you your instructions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me that personally. He ordered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you get a written order telling you what to do?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: An oral order.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did Pandurevic say it to you himself or did someone else convey it to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It was conveyed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I was just told that we were going to Gostilja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Simsic, where was he at this time? Was he also in Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. He was in town. He was a police officer. If you're referring to Simsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think I mean Goran Ristic. Is that the man who went to the village with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was in Rujiste too. We were there together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from you two, was anybody else given the order to go down to Gostilja and to speak with these people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us, as best you can recall, precisely what was your order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Our order wasn't there as such. It was just a piece of information that we were going to take the trucks and pick them up and they should take their belongings with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the trucks were -- whose trucks were they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Centrotrans's trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did you pick up the trucks? Did you go to the Centrotrans building or wherever it was located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, because they passed through my village. We waited for them there when they were on the way to Gostilja, because they had to pass that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you received your orders, did you receive it by somebody telling you who was present or did you receive it over a walkie-talkie, some kind of radio device?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, by a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have a Motorola that was assigned to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. In every trench there was one, one on ten people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you left to complete your order, your orders, did you take the Motorola with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did Ristic take a Motorola with him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Whose Lada Niva was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We used it for the army, but I don't know who it belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did it belong to a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I believe it belonged to the forestry company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you said that you went to the village of Gostilja the day before the people were picked up in the trucks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then I returned home. I spent the night there and then I went there with the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who did you go with to the village of Gostilja the day before the people left in the trucks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: With Ristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: By foot, from Prelovo, and by truck to Prelovo, with our truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Are you saying that you went from Rujiste to Prelovo on foot?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: From Rujiste to Prelovo by truck; from Prelovo to my home on foot, to Gostilja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far it is from Prelovo to Gostilja by foot?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Three, three and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you armed when you went to Gostilja that night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was Ristic armed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did either one of you have a Motorola at that stage?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you say to the people in the village on that night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It wasn't night; it was daytime. We told them that we had been informed to inform them that those who so wished should be prepared tomorrow and that the trucks would be coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that the people were not required to leave the next day; they were just being offered a -- they were being offered transportation out of the village if they so decided or desired to leave the village? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't done by force. Who wanted to would go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG117, she says that she knows you by Cira Djuric, and you've told us that your name -- or that people do know you by the name Cira. Do you have any doubt that she is describing you when she describes two men coming to her village the day before they left?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I withdraw that question. Had you ever been to this village before the day that you told these people that transportation would be provided for them? Were you ever there before that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: You mean during the war or before?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I mean in just the few days prior to the day that you collected these people in the truck.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG117 said that you were there on a number of occasions looking or asking about men in the village. Were you ever there asking about the whereabouts of men in the village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What village is Ristic from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Djurovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where is that with respect to Loznica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Below Rujiste, near the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Going from the village of Gostilja, would they be in the same direction or opposite directions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go after you left the village of Gostilja the day before the people left?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you told the people that tomorrow you would be there with trucks to transport them out of there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did Ristic go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. We spent the night there and we waited for him that morning, next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ristic went to your house in Loznica and stayed there the night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you know that the Centrotrans trucks would come to your house and pick you up?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Because they pass next to my house. That is the direction they pursue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know that they would stop and pick you up the next day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They had to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did they have to stop?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Because they knew that we would be waiting for them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If these people were simply being offered a ride, why was it necessary for you to return to the village the next morning?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: For safety. That was the order. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You say for safety. Is it your understanding that you were to protect these people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. In any case, that was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If your job was to protect these people, why did you not stay in their village and protect them? Why did you leave them unprotected and then return the next morning?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The commander knows that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the commander tell you not to stay at the village to protect Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. these people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There was no need for us to protect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So if there's no need for you to protect them, doesn't that contradict what you've just told us, that you were there to protect them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It is a large village. We couldn't just the two of us protect it, protect the whole village. Our position wasn't there. It was in Rujiste, much further away. We weren't able to protect all the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So is it your testimony today that your order was to protect these people, but because the village was so large, you and Ristic decided you couldn't protect them and you went to your home and you both went to your home in Loznica? Is that your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't go to protect them, just to inform them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, if your job wasn't to protect them, let me ask my initial question again: Why did you have to go on the Centrotrans truck to the village the next day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, I was told to do so, to help out, to see what they needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "to help out, to see what they needed", when you say "they," do you mean the other people on the trucks or the villagers in Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The villagers of Gostilja. I'm referring to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So are you telling us now that parts of your orders were to go and to see what the people of Gostilja needed and to take care of what they needed? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: To help the old people. There were those that weren't able to be present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, is it not a fact that some of the people in Gostilja have cars?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. They used to have cars, but those who had cars had left earlier. Only the old people remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When the Centrotrans truck stops at your house and picks you up, can you describe for us how many people were already on those Centrotrans trucks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: When they were leaving Gostilja, when they were leaving Gostilja, then they stopped by.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you saying that you weren't at Gostilja in the morning when the people boarded the trucks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm asking when the truck picked you up in the morning before it went to Gostilja. You said the truck picked you up at your house, and what I'm asking you is: Who was in the trucks at that stage? Were there other Serbs in the truck at that stage?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. Only benches.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from the drivers of the three trucks, was there anybody else in the cabs or anywhere in those trucks, aside from the drivers of those trucks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you get or where did you first see the Lada Niva on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In Gostilja, at Miloje's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you got into one of the Centrotrans trucks, did Ristic get into the same truck or into another truck?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Into the same truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Centrotrans company, do you know whether that is owned by a Muslim or a Serb?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that, because I didn't work in Visegrad. I don't know who the manager was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened as soon as you got to the village of Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Nothing happened. The people had already gathered. I mean, they were -- some people were still arriving while we waited.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you walk around the village to see if anybody was still in their house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I walked only to VG117's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did Ristic also walk around the village looking for people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was Ristic when you walked to the home of VG117?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: He was near the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from you and Ristic, were there any other armed men in the village that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you go to VG117's house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Because of her mother-in-law. She was unable to come down the stairs by herself. That's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how did you know this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Because she had told me that when she was near the truck. She told me that her mother-in-law couldn't make it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Her mother-in-law didn't want to come or that she wasn't able to climb the stairs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. She wanted to come but she couldn't, and that is why we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, all of the people that wanted to leave Gostilja on this day, did they all happen to be Muslim people or did any Serb people also ask you to give them this ride to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did any of the Muslims in the village say to you, "Well, thank you, but I think I'll stay and return to their home"? Did any of the Muslims do that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it just so happened that this voluntary transportation out of the town, that all of the Muslims accepted your offer and all of the Serbs declined your offer; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, the Serbs were not moving out; only Muslims were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the Muslims were moving out because they wanted to move out, is what you're telling us here today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. Not because they wanted but because of the politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you realise that many people in the world consider this ethnic cleansing. Do you yourself consider what you did that day, do you consider it ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I wonder whether he should be given some form of a warning before he answers a question such as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll leave that to the Court's -- the Chamber's discretion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What's the Rule about whether he has to answer it or not? There is one. I just can't remember the number of it at the moment. 90(E), it is. If I gave him a warning that he was entitled to object to answering it, the next question would be whether we would compel him to answer the question, and I wonder where we're getting to with this line of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, I would ask -- the Prosecution would ask the Court to advise him that he does have the right to make the objection and then maybe cross that bridge depending on his answer. It may be unnecessary to discuss that at this juncture.
