utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But where are we going with this, Mr. Groome? You're entitled to test his evidence to the hilt, certainly, but why do we need to know his view about what other people are doing or perhaps what he is doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, my position would be that it would certainly go to his credit if he believed that he was involved in the commission of a crime against these people, and I would be encouraging the Court to disregard his testimony regarding the remainder of his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Bearing in mind his answers to so many of the questions so far, I wonder if it's necessary for that. But Mr. Domazet, have you got the Rules in front of you there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I haven't at this moment, but I know this, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What do you suggest? He's your witness. Should we warn him, and if so, what is your attitude to compelling him to answer it if he declines to answer it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my suggestion would be maybe to ask the witness, see if he can answer the question. You can warn him and advise him that he's not obliged to answer the question, but maybe he is in a position to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then. Sir, you, as a witness here, have a -- what is called a privilege to refuse to answer any question which may tend to incriminate you. You are being asked whether what you were doing -- you consider that what you were doing amounted to ethnic cleansing. Whilst that rather vague phrase has been bandied about now for some ten years, I don't know whether we can say for certain how it should be interpreted as a matter of law, but it clearly would, in my view, incriminate you if you agreed that what you were doing amounted to ethnic cleansing. Now, as I say, you have the right to refuse to answer that question upon the basis that you may incriminate yourself if you answer it. Do you understand what I'm trying to say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, do you wish to object to answering the question upon that basis -- the question was: Sir, you realise that many people in the world consider this ethnic cleansing. Do you yourself consider that what you did that day, do you consider it ethnic cleansing? Do you wish to object to answering that question on the basis that your answer may incriminate you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm afraid you have to answer one question or the other. If you say you do not wish to object to it, then I will tell you to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, that was not ethnic cleansing. It was a kind of help. I went there to help those people, not to kill or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The degree of ethnic cleansing to which I think Mr. Groome is referring is that you were forcibly moving those people from their homes, not killing them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Like I said, I didn't go there on my own, of my own free will, but pursuant to an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm afraid that still isn't an answer to the question. If you answer the question that you think it was forcibly removing those people from their homes, that may well incriminate you. Now, do you wish to object to answering the question, if that is what is involved in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, Mr. Groome, I have to say, I don't really think his answer to the question will add to the quality of his evidence or detract from the quality of his evidence, as it has already been demonstrated. It's a matter for you. Do you want us to compel him to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not at this time, Your Honour. If I could just ask a few related questions and see where it may lead us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I should hasten to add, as I understand it, everywhere else except perhaps in your own country, an objection based upon the fifth amendment cannot be used in order to draw unfavourable inferences.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's the understanding of the laws that exist in my country, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I thought that they did draw unfavourable inferences. But anyway, you proceed with some other line of questioning now. I don't think we'll get any further with this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know a woman by the name of Hajra Ramic from Medeze. And I will spell that. The village is M-e-d-e-z-e.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That village, do you know where that village is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: What village?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Medeze, M-e-d-e-z-e.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I've heard of that village, but I've never been there. It is in the direction of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you never went to that village, and once again, offered some help to the people in that village, or the Muslims in that village, to leave their homes there? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. No, except for Gostilja, I didn't go anyplace else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the Vuk Karadzic school, that wasn't near the front line of conflict in any way, was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry. Let me just ask a question about back in Gostilja. Were you given any instructions as to what you were to do if a Muslim family or any family declined the offer of a ride away from Gostilja? Were you to report that to anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It was up to them to decide. They decided on their own, because they had expressed a wish to move out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is: According to your orders, as you understood them, were you to report any people that did not leave the village, people that decided to remain?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who were you to report the names of these people who remained to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: To the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So in order to be able to -- I'm sorry. Strike that. Were you just to report the names of the Muslim people that remained or all the people, regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We've lost all the interpretation. I think you'll have to ask him the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My question to you -- your answer wasn't interpreted, so I'm going to ask you the question again and ask you to repeat your answer. Were you just to report the names of the Muslim people who remained or of all the people that remained?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, it was not my duty. I didn't have that responsibility. That was not the task that had been given to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you saying that you did not have the task of reporting who remained in the village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, just moments ago, didn't you say that you had the duty to report that to your command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You didn't say that here just moments ago, that you had this duty?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: There was no request to establish any statistics, to make a record of all those who had gathered. We didn't walk around the village, we didn't visit the houses, except for the home of VG117, to see who was left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The village of Drulje spelled D-r-u-l-j-e, are you familiar where that village is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It forms part of Gostilja, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how about the village of Vlahovici, V-l-a-h-o-v-i-c-i?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know Vlahovici, but it is further away, away from Gostilja. There was no one from Vlahovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever go to the village of Vlahovici and assist those people, or those Muslims, in leaving their home?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was your understanding of your responsibilities at the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I understood them in a moral sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have any specific instructions from your commander regarding what you were to do at the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did you understand your duties to be in the moral sense?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: In the sense that that was the way I should treat those people. It was not their responsibility. They were not guilty of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, maybe -- help me understand this fact. If your command has given you a specific instruction to help these people being transported from their village into town and you have no specific instructions regarding after that, isn't it your duty then to return to your command and resume your duties as before?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: My duty was to be there until further orders. I was taken back to the line the next day, and the others remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet asked you the following question, and you gave the following answer, and I want to ask you a question after I repeat this: "Q. Were there also other people that came from town and who were also participating?" And you said yes. Did you mean that other people came from town to the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Other people came, but on foot. They came to inquire about the convoy, about the departure time, because apparently they wanted to join it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So the people that you were referring to in response to Mr. Domazet's question were all Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Domazet asked you about your best memory regarding when -- or what day this happened, and you spoke about harvest time. I want to put the same question to you in another way. Did this occur before or after St. Vidovdan Day, the Serb Orthodox holiday?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when St. Vitus Day is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Even if you don't recall the precise day of the holiday, are you able to tell us whether what you've described to us today occurred before that holiday or after that holiday?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you should look at the transcript there, because the two of you are using a different word. It certainly sounded differently when he said it. I'm not sufficiently familiar with any of those holidays to be able to say that they -- you are both referring to the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise. I'll clear that up now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is St. Vitus Day also known as Vidovdan Day, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Like I said, I don't know the date of the holiday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Domazet could help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, I know you've given us a list, and I haven't got it with me at the moment. Are they both known as the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Vidovdan is the 28th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it the same as St. Vitus Day?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I think yes. Yes, they're the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, VG117, when she testified, said that some of the people at the school were then brought to the fire brigade in town, do you recall any people being brought to the fire brigade in town?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when policemen or any Serbs came to the school and brought some of the people anywhere, just brought them away from the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: While I was there, no, no one came.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it your responsibility to prevent any of these people from leaving the compound of the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. I was only told that they could go out to buy things for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who told you that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That is what the command told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And at this stage you still do not have a Motorola; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How does your command tell you that the people are allowed to come and go from the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The command was located in school, but not in the building of the elementary school, but in the secondary school. That is where they were quartered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you talking about your command or are you talking about another command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about my command, the main command.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you talking about the school here in Visegrad town or a school somewhere up in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: The local office was in Prelovo, but the main command was in the secondary school in Visegrad. These schools are close to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And somebody from that command came over and said to you that you were allowed to let the people come and go; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they asked to go themselves, to buy themselves something. They weren't locked up or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And before you allowed them to go, did you check with your command to see if you were allowed to let them go and buy things?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They moved around quite normally throughout the town, wherever they wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But sir, you've told us that your instructions from your command were that they were allowed to leave. When did you receive those instructions, and who -- or precisely what were those instructions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, we told them that as soon as we informed them, and we were informed to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When were you informed to do so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: While I was still in Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you were told in Rujiste: Bring them to the school, stay there until further instructions, and the people can leave if they want. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, VG117 saw a person she learned to be Milan Lukic. Do you know who Milan Lukic is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I've heard of him, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the time you were at the school, did anybody come to the school and address the people there and identify himself as Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: During the two days I was there, no one came. Afterwards, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, VG117 also described for us a certificate of safety that she received from the police commander by the name of Tomic. Had you ever heard or seen of these certificates of safety?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The people who were gathered in the school, did you check any of their identification papers or any of the papers that they had with them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG117 described for us a person whose name she knew as Cacanin and says that he was also present at the school when she was brought there. My question to you is: Do you know this person, and did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know him. I didn't see him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG117 also told us about a conversation she had with Rade Dikic. Do you know a person by that name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. He's from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And she said that Rade Dikic told her that the White Eagles, the same paramilitary group that you've told us you heard was in Visegrad, that they were there according to a plan and they were implementing a plan. Were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know what they were saying. I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that about the White Eagles, that they were there according to a plan?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard the name White Eagles, but whether they had a plan or not, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, VG117 says it wasn't Mr. Simsic who brought her to the school, but rather, Miloje, and you testified that you know about Mr. Joksimovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I know him. She spent the night in his house, because the Niva was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it him who brought her mother-in-law to the school or was it Goran Ristic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It was Goran Ristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why is it that the people who were going to leave town on this convoy, why was it they were not assembled at the bus station or at the centre of town but they were brought to this school at the edge of town?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I don't know. That was the order issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In response to a question of Mr. Domazet, you said that people would come during the night. Did you mean that people would come to the school during the night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Someone coming to school at night? I don't know who came to school during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that no one came to the school at night; is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No one, until 10.00 or 11.00. People would come and go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the police ever come to the school at night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. They patrolled during the night, day. They would come, look, and then they would go elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were these local police that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They were reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: They were police reservists or army reservists?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Police reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were they from Visegrad or from outside of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: From Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how many times during the night did these police reservists come to the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they would come several times, to see the town, to spend seven or eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did they actually enter the school during the night?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it a fact that on the day that you brought these people to Visegrad, that Mitar Vasiljevic was in fact in front of the school, at a desk, recording the names of the people before they entered the school? Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No. No one recorded the names, nor was there anyone there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you count the number of people that were there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So this convoy that was coming the next morning, nobody was interested in knowing how many people were asking to leave Visegrad on the convoy so that they could determine how many buses or trucks to bring?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, there were about a hundred. I don't know the exact number. Because people from town would come. They would inquire. And people from surrounding villages would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, prior to agreeing to come here to testify, you asked for a guarantee from the Chamber that you would not be arrested or charged with a crime while you were here testifying; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You never made such a request from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was asked, but I didn't make that demand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djuric, in response to Mr. Groome's question about the time when you were mobilised, you associated that with the departure of the Uzice Corps, but according to what has been answered and recorded, it was mentioned that this was in April. My question is: Can you remember whether the Uzice Corps really left in April or in some other month?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I think it was in April. I don't -- I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. You can't remember that. Do you associate your mobilisation and departure with the time of departure of the Uzice Corps, whenever that was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Well, I will repeat the question in a different way. Regardless of when the Uzice Corps left, because you cannot remember the date, is it true that you were mobilised in that time, or, in other words, at the time when the Uzice Corps left, and that you were then mobilised and did the things that you have described to us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: That is correct, because at the time, the mobilisation was not in progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does it mean that a mobilisation of others and of yourself only began when the Uzice Corps left?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In response to Mr. Groome's question when you spoke of the supplies to the front line somewhere in Rujiste, where you yourself were, you mentioned a kombi van and the name of the driver, that his name was Obren Vojnovic. The question was: Who was with him? And you said you didn't know. My question to you is: Do you not know that because you did not know those people, or you were not in a position to see who, along with the driver of the van, were bringing food supplies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: We were not in a position, because we did not actually -- we were in inaccessible places, in brooks. Then they would bring food, then it would be empty. Who was riding, driving, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. In response to Mr. Groome's question about the vehicle and the colour of the vehicle, you spoke of one colour at one time and another colour at another time, and the colour, the subsequent colour, does it relate to this time or some other time? Did the colour change in some other time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, the van exists now. It is red and is used to transfer the workers employed in Sumarstvo, in the forestry enterprises

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In response to Mr. Groome's question about Gostilja and the behaviour of the people and how they understood what you were doing, you provided some explanations, but I ask you to be more specific. My question would be: Did you require all Muslims from the village to go along with you in those trucks? Was that the demand? Or were the inhabitants allowed to remain if they so desired?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, no one was forced to go; only those wishing to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: From the people that were with you, did you hear from them why would these people wish to leave their homes at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, they wished to go to Tuzla. That was their wish. Because it was safer for them, because it became a Muslim territory, without Serbs. They felt safer while the political war was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: From your side or anyone's side, your side, whether it was said to them that they were definitely moving, or was it done differently?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It wasn't ordered? It wasn't an order? They weren't ordered to leave?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, I wasn't referring to that, whether they had to or not, but the question is whether at the time they were talking amongst themselves, whether they would leave their houses definitely or only temporarily and that they would eventually return to their homes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: I was told that they should be told to find provisional accommodations, because the young people had already left and only the old people remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you said young people left, does that mean that there were no young people in the village left at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you know where they had gone, these young people, and when they left?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They went into the forest, into the woods, with guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you said that those that remained were scared and wished to leave, who were they scared of? Did they say something about this to you, or do you know something about it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They weren't so scared and didn't say they were scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that they also expressed a wish to go to areas that were predominantly populated by Muslims. Did they say why?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They wished to move somewhere where it was safe, temporarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Well, my question was - and you didn't answer it - why did they feel that it was not safe for them in Gostilja, that it wasn't safe for them to remain there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't safe because they were near the border with Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that the fact that they were near the border with Serbia, that there were people from Serbia who were coming from Serbia and who could endanger them or could endanger them [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that refer to what you said when you spoke about illegal units or an illegal army, that those were people who came from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In response to some questions of Mr. Groome's referring to Mr. Joksimovic, it was said that VG117 had slept overnight there on the way to the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a neighbour there. There were three or four Serb homes, and all the rest were Muslim homes. And she spent the night at his house and then she continued to Zaovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that Miloje Joksimovic's house was in that village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: It was in the village of Gostilja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know whether they went to the Serb village, the village in Serbia that you mentioned? Did they take a car or did you go on foot [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They went on foot, because there's no road there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know how far this is in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: About two or three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: One question in respect of the first day when you went to Gostilja. In response to Mr. Groome's question, you said that it wasn't in the night, in the evening; it was in the day. But you didn't say what time of the day, what part of the day. What part of the day did you go with Ristic to inform them that trucks would be coming?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: About 10.00 or -- 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And the following day, besides going to the home of VG117, did all the other people go by themselves to the place where the trucks were parked?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DJURIC
utterances.text: They came by themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I have no other questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir, for coming to give your evidence and for the evidence that you have given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Domazet, your next witness, I understand, you want protective measures for. What number are we up to with your pseudonyms?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, that it will be VGD24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 24. Yes. And facial distortion, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, only facial and -- no voice. No voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Have you got any problems with that, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The witness that starts tomorrow morning will be Witness VGD24. Tomorrow afternoon. I hope that by tomorrow afternoon they will do something about the air conditioning in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, a couple of administrative matters to take care of. Before the break the Chamber had asked us to provide a redacted copy of Exhibit 113A, the report of Dr. Broeders. I will tender that now into evidence. I will also ask the Court, I think there's some confusion as to whether 113 is under seal. If it isn't, maybe it would be sensible to place that under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Shall we give this the same number but with a 1 after it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. I think we marked it 113A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well, then. Exhibit 113 will be under seal, if it is not already so, and the redacted version will be Exhibit 113A. Have the passages that you have redacted from been noted on any B/C/S version of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't believe there is a B/C/S version of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Isn't there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll check that Your Honour, and have an answer tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will probably be the first exhibit that hasn't had a B/C/S version. But if there has been, it might be a good idea just to mark it up on it, so there can be no doubt on the part of the Defence which parts they should refer to in public and which they should not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There's one other matter, it's regarding the frequency of blood type A-plus in the normal population. The Prosecution, using the Internet, has got that information from a blood bank. I've shown it to Mr. Domazet, and we were prepared to enter into an agreement that the blood type A-plus, that its frequency in the population is 32.3 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I knew it would be very large. It is the largest one, as I understand it. But when you say "plus," you mean blood type A RH positive. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. We had better get it straight. It certainly is the largest group.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: According to this, it isn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Isn't it? Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: RH plus is 38.4 per cent, so it's the second largest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps things have changed since I had to worry about these things. Perhaps that is why there are so many other systems other than the A, B, C, O. We'll resume tomorrow at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
